s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic unilateral eyelid swelling with discharge
salient_findings: 2-year history of swelling of the right upper eyelid
Immovable scarlike node on the right upper eyelid
Ring enhancement in the right frontal sinus on MRI
key_facts: 52-year-old Japanese woman
2-year history of swelling of the right upper eyelid
Discharge of pus for 10 months
No trauma to the head
Otherwise healthy
No fever, headache, or nasal discharge
Immovable scarlike node, 11 × 7 mm, on the right upper eyelid
High signal on T2-weighted MRI and ring enhancement in the right frontal sinus
Opacification of the right frontal, ethmoid, and maxillary sinuses on CT
Expansion of the right frontal and ethmoid sinuses without bone destruction
Mild inflammatory infiltrate with fibrosis and lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate on histopathology

shortlist.label: Chronic dacryocystitis
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic unilateral eyelid swelling with discharge, consistent with blockage of the nasolacrimal duct

shortlist.label: Frontal sinus mucocele
shortlist.why_kept: Imaging studies showing opacification and expansion of the right frontal sinus, consistent with a mucocele

shortlist.label: Pott's puffy tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic discharge and swelling of the eyelid, with imaging studies showing frontal sinus involvement

shortlist.label: IgG4-related disease
shortlist.why_kept: Mild inflammatory infiltrate with fibrosis and lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate on histopathology, consistent with IgG4-related disease

shortlist.label: Actinomycosis
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic discharge and swelling of the eyelid, with imaging studies showing sinus involvement, consistent with actinomycosis

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of a swelling on the right upper eyelid with discharge of pus, combined with imaging findings of opacification and expansion of the right frontal and ethmoid sinuses, and the absence of trauma or other symptoms, is most consistent with Pott's puffy tumor, a rare complication of frontal sinusitis.

rejected.label: Chronic dacryocystitis
rejected.why: The lack of symptoms related to the nasolacrimal duct and the specific involvement of the frontal sinus suggest this is not the primary issue.

rejected.label: Frontal sinus mucocele
rejected.why: While mucoceles can cause expansion of the sinuses, the presence of pus discharge and the specific clinical presentation point more towards an infectious or inflammatory process like Pott's puffy tumor.

rejected.label: IgG4-related disease
rejected.why: The histopathology findings do not specifically support IgG4-related disease, which typically shows a dense lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate with a high percentage of IgG4-positive plasma cells.

rejected.label: Actinomycosis
rejected.why: Actinomycosis can cause chronic suppurative infections, but the specific involvement of the frontal sinus and the clinical presentation are more suggestive of Pott's puffy tumor, a known complication of sinusitis.
